text: Warren Buffett has a recession signal.
Wall Street calls it the Buffett Indicator.
It compares total US stock market value to GDP.
Buffett himself called it the best single measure of market valuation.
When it crossed two hundred percent before the dotcom crash, anyone who bought the S and P that year didn't break even until two thousand seven. Seven years of nothing.
Right now, every public stock in America is worth more than double the entire economy. Two hundred and nine percent.
The only other times this ratio has been this high, the next decade was flat or negative.
Buffett's response is the same as it was then. Record cash at Berkshire — over three hundred and eighty billion dollars.
Not buying the index. Not rotating into bonds. Sitting in cash, waiting for prices to come to him.
